note: RIGHTS: applied the settled DASS row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv (verdict=ship, Ben 2026-09-10) -- the Psychology Foundation of Australia's DASS FAQ states "The DASS questionnaire is public domain, and so permission is not needed to use it. The DASS questionnaires and scoring key may be downloaded from the DASS website and copied without restriction" (http://www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass/DASSFAQ.htm, page sha256 a4800f9439e4828d57c4bcd243e4a848b50c404740cae05d4990c2a77bd638b5). Not re-derived. LANGUAGE: administered in English -- the paper's Methods say outright "The English version has been used in the study" (Jakarta, Indonesia sample; online Google Forms) -- so no language / _translated columns. TEXT: transcribed verbatim from the official Dass21.pdf on the DASS site (instructions, the four rating-scale anchors, all 21 items), keeping its own spellings and parentheticals ("(eg, in the hands)", "a good part of time"); the form's two-line item wraps were joined with a single space and nothing else was altered. The paper itself reproduces no item wording. MAPPING: data/xiong_2025_dass21.py melts the S2 File .xlsx columns DASS_1..DASS_21 BY NAME (DASS_ITEMS = [f"DASS_{i}" for i in range(1,22)]), so the IRW code IS the source column name and nothing can shift between source and IRW -- but those headers carry no wording, so tying code number n to DASS-21 item n is still an inference from the instrument's published item order: hence paper_order, not data_labels. What supports it documentarily is the paper's own Methods, which assigns the canonical DASS-21 numbering to this study's items ("Depression (items 3, 5, 10, 13, 16, 17, 21), Anxiety (items 2, 4, 7, 9, 15, 19, 20) and Stress (items 1, 6, 8, 11, 12, 14, 18)") and quotes the 0 and 3 anchors; and its Table 2, whose per-item Mean(SD)/skewness/kurtosis for I1..I21 (Wave 1, n=519) reproduce the .xlsx columns DASS_1..DASS_21 row for row to 2 dp, so the paper's item numbers denote these columns. Checked against the data in Step 5b, PARTIAL. RESP: 0-3 with the printed anchors; the live resp set is exactly 0,1,2,3 and the paper quotes 0 = "did not apply to me at all" and 3 = "applied to me very much or most of the time", matching the official form's direction, so no raw_resp fallback was needed.
public_note: The DASS-21 instructions and 0-3 anchors shipped for this table are the official paper form's wording ("Please read each statement and circle a number 0, 1, 2 or 3"); Xiong et al. administered the scale online through Google Forms, so respondents selected rather than circled a number. The item wording is the same official form's, verbatim.
